what: Amphenol makes connectors, cables, antennas and sensors, the parts that carry power and data inside everything from fighter jets and cars to AI servers.
customers: Makers of data-centre equipment, cars, aircraft, defence systems, phones and industrial machines.
money: high-speed connectors and cables for data centres and networks
rugged connectors for defence, aerospace and industry
sensors and assemblies, much of it for cars
moat: A decentralised structure of many small, fast units, parts designed into customers' products, and a long record of acquisitions.
risks: A slowdown in AI data-centre spending
opportunities: Revenue grew about 52% last year on data centre connector demand
Operating margin of 25% with return on invested capital of 15%
Analysts see about 38% upside from current levels
watch: Data centre and communications connector revenue growth.
